spec_match.rationale: A path routed with race-network-and-fetch-handler, with a genuinely slow network side (a server route that paces its chunks) and a worker side whose delay the page controls. The winner of each race is read from a response header.

interactive.rationale: Three controls, a single-race button and a sweep that runs nine handler delays and draws the crossover.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The page says racing doubles requests and that the crossover measured on localhost is a localhost number.

edge_cases.rationale: An uncontrolled page; a sweep where one side wins at every delay, which is described rather than assumed away.

references.rationale: chromestatus.com/feature/5194817700364288 and the addRoutes specification section.

conformance.rationale: Three concept-level assertions: fetch resolves on headers rather than on the body (the finding this page rests on), the slow-stream fixture is actually slow, and custom headers survive a synthesised Response.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Measured in Chrome 150 across a nine-point sweep: the worker wins at a delay of 0ms and the network wins from 20ms upward, with headers arriving at 1–3ms while the body takes ~167ms.

telemetry_health.rationale: Emits every race with its handler delay, timings and winner, and the whole sweep.

design_system.rationale: CSS variables, button colour pairs, 44px controls, table in its own scroll container.

accessibility.rationale: Winners are text; the sweep rungs carry their values beside the bars; results announced through aria-live.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Control grid auto-fits; rung rows use fixed narrow label columns; the table scrolls in its own container.

openQuestions.title: The crossover measured here is a localhost crossover
openQuestions.detail: A race is settled by whichever side produces a response, and a streamed response exists as soon as its headers do — so the network wins on a time-to-first-byte of one or two milliseconds even though its body takes 160ms. Repeating the sweep against a throttled connection would produce the number a real application should reason about.

guidanceConsulted.query: announce results of a swept measurement
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Announce the conclusion of a multi-run sweep in a live region rather than leaving the reader to interpret a chart.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The sweep writes a sentence naming the crossover and what it was racing against; every rung also carries its own duration and winner as text.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: deno task drive asserts the crossover sentence mentions time to first byte.

summary: Two measurement bugs found by the page's own output: a query parameter spelled `delay` instead of `delayMs`, which made the slow side finish in under a millisecond, and the assumption that a race is decided by which side finishes rather than which side responds.
